title: Minimum Number of Coins for Fruits
prompt: You are visiting a farm with `n` fruits lined up, indexed from `1` to `n`. The `i`-th fruit (1-indexed) has a price `prices[i - 1]`. The farm has a special offer: if you buy the `i`-th fruit at its price, you can get the next `i` fruits for free. Note offers can stack and overlap: even a fruit you got for free can still trigger its own free offer if you additionally choose to buy it. Return the minimum number of coins needed to acquire all `n` fruits.

examples.explanation: Buy the 1st fruit for 3 coins, which makes the 2nd fruit free. Then buy the 2nd fruit anyway (it's free, so 0 extra... but to also unlock its free offer you'd pay again); optimal here is buy fruit 1 (3 coins, get fruit 2 free), then buy fruit 3 for 1 coin: total 3 + 1 = 4.
Buy the 1st fruit for 1 coin to get the 2nd free. Buy the 3rd fruit for 1 coin to get the 4th free. Total is 2 coins.
With a single fruit, you must simply buy it; there's no later fruit for its offer to make free.

hints: This isn't simple greedy scanning — whether buying fruit i is worth it depends on optimal decisions for fruits after it, so think dynamic programming.

Define dp[i] as the minimum coins needed to acquire all fruits from i through n. From fruit i, you must pay prices[i-1], and that grants fruits i+1..2i free, so you only need to fund dp[j] for the best j > i to continue from (you're never forced to skip ahead, you can also just consider continuing from i+1).

dp[i] = prices[i-1] + min over j in [i+1, min(2*i, n)+1] of dp[j], with dp[n+1] = 0. Take the answer as dp[1], iterating i from n down to 1, and also allow continuing from i+1 if that's cheaper than jumping further (include j = i+1 in the min range).

solution.approach: Use dynamic programming where dp[i] is the minimum cost to acquire fruits i through n (1-indexed), with dp[n+1] = 0. To acquire fruit i you must pay prices[i-1] (buying it is unavoidable to make progress from position i), which frees fruits i+1 through i+i. After that purchase you may resume purchasing from any position j between i+1 and min(2i, n) + 1 — not necessarily the very end of the free range, since sometimes it's cheaper to buy an already-free fruit early to unlock its own larger offer. So dp[i] = prices[i-1] + min(dp[j] for j in i+1..min(2i,n)+1). Compute dp from i = n down to 1 and return dp[1].
solution.code:
def minimum_coins(prices):
    n = len(prices)
    dp = [0] * (n + 2)
    for i in range(n, 0, -1):
        best_next = min(dp[j] for j in range(i + 1, min(2 * i, n) + 2))
        dp[i] = prices[i - 1] + best_next
    return dp[1]
solution.timeComplexity: O(n^2) worst case (can be optimized to O(n log n) with a sliding-window minimum structure)
